utterances.text: No. Much as the state of national necessity was considered temporary, so did the law define all administrative activities of the police put in force by the new law for the duration of such a state of immediate threat of war or of war. Upon cessation of such states, the police no longer has the right to use them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to be able to understand what the issue at hand is, I wanted to direct you to footnote 20 of your expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In e-court, it is at pages 12 and 13 in the B/C/S; in the English, it is page 13 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me which are the most characteristic administrative activities foreseen by that law?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: According to the law you refer to, in my expert report, I singled out some characteristic situations of revised or added administrative activities. I stipulated them in the footnote. In item 1, it is enforcing a special regime of accessing or leaving an object that is of security interest. This is not included in the basic law. This is a completely new activity. Another activity or authority is enforcing a special traffic regime for motor vehicles in designated locations, which is also a completely new administrative activity. Activity number 3 is prohibiting the carrying and use of weapons and ammunition including explosive substances in public places except for authorised personnel. If used in accordance with the rules of service, this administrative activity had existed before. The fourth one is prohibiting the sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages in public places. This is a brand new administrative activity. Item 5, suspending the transport and trade of weapons and explosive substances in designated locations except for the needs of the army and the MUP. It was a somewhat modified administrative activity compared to the regular activities. Under 6, ordering persons to reside in a designated place or prohibiting them to leave a designated place with mandatory reporting to the police. This was a new administrative activity not envisaged by the peacetime law. 7, prohibiting the crossing of the state border. Save for a narrow category of certain persons, this was a new activity. Under 8, terminating the sojourn of certain categories of persons, a new administrative activity. Then next is 9, taking specific measures against certain persons which impact the inviolability of personal rights. Here what is included is, for example, detaining and apprehending persons. Item 10 is taking specific measures without a previous written notice being served. That is an amended activity. The next one is ordering the measure of detention of persons, as well as searching places of residence, including a possible use of firearms; that is to say, police officers participating in such an activity need to have their firearms ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was footnote 20. I believe, in e-court, we did not have the proper page displayed. This is a good time for the break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's 12 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know. I heard you say that, I note. Is there a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just on page 47, line 9, it just said footnote 20 appears in English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Let me get to page 47 because we are on page 49. Yes, line 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It says that footnote 20 of his report appears on page 13 in English; it's actually just page 10. I think that's what they wanted to talk about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The difference is the pages in e-court do not correspond to the actual report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Thank you for that. We'll have a 20 minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bajagic, I have just completed with one section of your report before the break. Now I would like to move on to chapter 2 in your report, and that is Establishment and Development of the MUP of Republika Srpska. We are going to go more quickly through this topic. In the subsection entitled "General Framework," that's page 39 -- actually, item 39; and on page 14 in English. You mentioned a large number of documents and events that in your view were particularly important in 1991 and 1992, and the crisis in Bosnia. I am not going to go with you through the entire report of yours. Based on item 39, can you tell us please in your opinion which circumstances had decisive impact on the establishment of MUP of the then-Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was later on transformed into the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Well, this is a list of documents that deal with the general political situation in the former Yugoslavia and Bosnia-Herzegovina; and within this context, we might highlight some documents that, inter alia, had had an impact on the creation of the first outline of the Ministry of the Interior of the present Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your view, what was the significance of Cutileiro's plan, and particular the fact that the then-president of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic, abandoned this plan?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Well, Cutileiro's plan in the lengthy process before it was finally adopted certainly constitutes a basis that all the political protagonists that here to as the basis for setting up their state administration organs including Ministry Of The Interior. Cutileiro's plan, according to the version that I had an opportunity to read, in its chapter (d) speaks about the right of the three entities in Bosnia-Herzegovina to establish administration organs, which included Ministry of the Interior as a separate organ. This plan had originally been endorsed by all the three parties involved in the crisis in Bosnia-Herzegovina. At any rate, the acceptance of the plan and then the abandonment of the plan of one party, i.e., Mr. Izetbegovic, certainly didn't go well down with the remaining two parties, and it had the impact that it had.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't think it's necessary that we look into Cutileiro's plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, I would like just to say that this is the document already in e-court and has previously been used in this court. That is document 4D169, and the translation version is 1D1156.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to hear your document -- to hear your comment on the document on 4D174; and in your binder, you will find it under tab 4. This is a dispatch sent by the collegium of MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina dated the 1st of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what this document is about. I would like to hear your comment.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: In short, this document speaks about a meeting of the expert collegium of the then-Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina, at which this Sarajevo plan was being discussed and the possible implementation of Cutileiro's plan, in terms of initiating a sort of decentralization of the Ministry of the Interior into three separate entities. In view of the structure of the personnel, it is noticeable that this meeting was attended by the highest official BH at the time, starting from the minister, his deputies, and all other officials who were members of the collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. If you look at the first part of this dispatch, can you tell me what were the general premises exercised by the members of the collegium of the then-Ministry of the Interior or BH?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: These general premises were that first phases or stages of re-organisation of MUP had already been underway; that's the main point. The collegium had been advised that certain legislative foundation had been laid for the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian side, i.e., the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraphs 46 to 53, pages 16 to 18 in your report in B/C/S, and pages 16 to 19 in English in e-court, you spoke about illegal arming of members of the SDS being one of the reasons conducive to the break-up of the MUP of the Bosnia-Herzegovina. In that respect, you analysed a number of documents and books which were listed in the footnotes. Can you just tell us briefly - I don't want to dwell on this too long - about this phenomenon. So I'm speaking about the arming of members about the SDA? How did this phenomenon affect the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: In any case, the reasons for the setting up of the MUP and consequently taking into account the Cutileiro's plan, although I don't think these were the only reasons that exacerbated the crisis, but one of the reason was definitely operational activities of all three parties, and I here mentioned only one of them. I analysed the reasons for establishing the first state organs of the future Republika Srpska, which was prompted by secret and illegal arming of certain formations in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991 and in spring of 1992. These facts could not have remained clandestine, and they definitely contributed to the worsening of the situation and prompted the initiation of the realisation of the plans to establish the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Further on, in your analysis, you spoke about the activities of the HDZ, which was the party of the Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and their aspirations towards political and every other separation from the central government in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is on pages 54 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please read the pages slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, the interpreters have kindly asked you to read out the pages slowly please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters; I didn't pay attention to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So these are pages 18 and 19 in e-court, in B/C/S; and 19 and 20 in the English version, also in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, is it necessary for me to repeat my question?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please give me an answer now?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: As you can read in certain paragraphs in my report, I focused my attention on the third party which had certain input in the generating of the crisis in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is, conditionally speaking, the Croatian party that I'm talking about. For me, it was particularly indicative because of the dates and years when the mention of first state organs were mentioned within the Croatian community, and particularly the mention of an existence of a source of Herceg Bosna in 1992, as well as the fact that they started forming their own units, like HVO and others. So, just as I was speaking about the authority Sarajevo, I also mentioned the aspirations of the Croatian community. So all of these aspects can be amalgamated to create a reason that precipitated the activities undertaken by the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now move to the next topic in your report, and that is the Creation and Development of MUP of Republika Srpska in the period 1991-1993. In your report, it is dealt with in paragraphs 60 to 91, and you and I will just go through a number of details. Can you please first look at paragraph 61 of your analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on page 20 in e-court, and on page 21 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Here you say that all the three ruling ethnic parties strove to exert as much influence as possible on the then-MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can you give us more details about what this refers to.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: In view of the interparty agreement that was reached in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time, at the highest level, the certain offices in state administration were allocated according to these percentage ratio. Based on this interparty agreement, for various reasons, this agreement was violated in that all three parties, by appointing their representatives in the MUP, strove to occupy the best possible position, and, thereby, have an opportunity to have a decisive impact on the policy of MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So that was a process that was concurrently aimed at personnel policy, and was pursued by all three parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Further on, you spoke about the filling of jobs in MUP and the departure of Muslims for training in Croatia. Can you tell me how did these processes affect the overall situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: As a state administration organ, the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina is part of the executive branch and is entitled to issue certain guidelines relating to personnel policy in the MUP. It is very indicative that political parties, and in this particular instance, the Party of Democratic Action, exerted a decisive influence on the administration for personnel of the Ministry of the Interior, and I illustrated this with a number of specific examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us look just at one such example.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's document 4D167, and if we can please have this document brought up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch sent to the Public Security station in Bratunac dated 16 March 1992, and that is tab 5 in your binder. Can you tell us what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: This document is one of the forms of passing on information at a higher level of organisation -- or rather, to a higher level of organisation compared to the Bratunac station. It speaks about a number of Muslims who had gone to undertake training -- or undergo training in Croatia organised by MUP of Croatia. The chief of the Public Security station said explicitly that he did not know upon whose orders or recommendations these men had gone to undergo training in the MUP of Croatia, and he also adds that the Serbs do not trust these people because they could be recruited for the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: It was signed Senad Hodzic, the then-chief of the Public Security station. This is as much as I can gather from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 74 of your expert analysis, it's on pages 23 to 25 in English, and 25 and 26. You enlisted some crucial regulations that governed the creation and the development of the MUP of Republika Srpska. Let us go through some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first document that I would like to show is 4D168.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And in your binder, it's tab 6. That's the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Let us look at chapter 4, Article 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's pages 5 and 6 in e-court in B/C/S, and in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us first look at the heading of this chapter. Can you tell us what is the heading of this chapter where Article 68 is?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: That's chapter 4 of the constitution of the Serbian Republika Srpska of Bosnia-Herzegovina of 1992, and it's entitled "The Rights and Duties of the Republic."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now move n to Article 68, item 2.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to Article 68, the obligation of the republic is to provide and to secure various arrangements or areas of life enumerated under numbers 1 to 15 and under number 2, defence and security of the republic is specified which is directly related to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Item 13 on the next page?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Item 13, the state should regulate and provide for the functioning of the competent governmental bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What is your understanding of the provisions we just looked at as regards the creation and organisation of the Ministry of the Interior in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: If the then-Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had the right to organise the activities in certain walks of life, we can see that they enumerated 15 of the most important such areas, much as would be in any other state. If they had such a right, then they also could get involved in the organisation, competence, and the work of such state agencies that have to do with security.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the Law on Government of the Republica of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina. In e-court, it's 4D173.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your binder it's tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at chapter 2, Article 6 on the Law on Government. It is page 6 in e-court in the B/C/S; in the English, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you have Article 6 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If we look at Article 6, item 1, what can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: We can see that, in keeping with Article 5, the government consists of the prime minister, two deputy prime ministers, and 13 members ministers. In Article 5, it is further stated that presidents of executive bodies, districts, and/or ex officio members of the government; and then we have the stipulation of all of the various areas of government that needs to have officials appointed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe you should repeat.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I can repeat, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which ministries are those that are being formed in the then-Republic of the Serbian People of the Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: There were 13 ministries. I can enumerate: First, Internal Affairs; then, National Defence; the Ministry of Justice; Finance; Foreign Affairs; Economic Affairs; Agriculture, Forestry, and Water Management --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I do not wish to interrupt, but --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Well, and so on and so forth. But I believe the first few are the most important ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us move on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 4D170. It is the Law on State Administration, dated the 23rd of March 1992. Let us have a look at chapter 4, Article 19. That is page 3 in the B/C/S version; in the English the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your binder, tab 8. Do you have the document before you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I do, but which article are you in?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Article 19.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What is regulated by Article 19?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Chapter 4, Organisation of Administrative Organs, Article 19, it says administrative organs shall be established as ministries, secretariats, and administrations; that is to say, the law foresaw three types of state bodies: Ministries, secretariats, and administrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As regards the field of Internal Affairs, was it also arranged according to this provision?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Together with the Law on the Government and the Law on Government Administration, these two pieces of legislation organised the -- rather, prescribed the organisation of the Ministry of the Interior of the then-Serbian Republic which is later to be dubbed Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is the Law on Defence which is 4D181.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tab 68 in your binder, dated the 1st of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The article that I want to focus on is in e-court at page 2 in the B/C/S, and pages 2 and 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It regulates -- well, first of all, Article 7, what does that regulate?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: If I may have a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What does it regulate in its introductory part?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Article 7, it's introductory part regulates certain areas which fall under the competence of the president of the Serbian republic of B&H, with regard to organising defence preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at item 3 of the article. What is the authority given to the president the of Serbian Republic of B&H?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Item 3 of Article 7, it states that is the president of the Serbian Republic of B&H operates and commands the army in peace and wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 6 of the same article is next. What does it regulate?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I've read it. The president has the right to define the basis for organisation and strength of the police force, issue orders for utilization of the police in case of war, imminent threat of war, in order to protect the rights and duties of the republic and its citizens and their duties and obligations accorded by the constitution. This presidential role has to do with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In this law, there is a mention of the Army of Republika Srpska. In keeping with this law, is the Ministry of the Interior mentioned as an element of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No, not in this law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now go to Article 10 of the law. It is on the same page in the B/C/S; in the English version, it is pages 3 and 4 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the bottom part of the article. There is a subheading, "Ministry of the Interior." Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What are the competences of the Ministry of the Interior according to this regulation that have to do with the defence of the republic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I can tell you right away. According to Article 10, the Ministry of the Interior is competent to organise and implement its own preparations for defence and work in a situation of an imminent threat of war or of war. It organises security measures and provides security for objects important for the defence, and organises preparations of the police in the state necessity, as defined here. These being the threat of war and state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us go next to some of the most important regulation concerning the police, and that is the Law on Internal Affairs. Could we next have 4D172 in e-court, Official Gazette, 4-92.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is tab 9. The date is 23 March 1992. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at Article 3 of the law. It is in e-court page 2 in the B/C/S; in the English version, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How does this law regulate the field of Internal Affairs in terms of police tasks?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: According to this article, and as part of this law, the role of the police is the following: Tasks and activities relating to public security, tasks and activities related to national security, as well as tasks and activities relating to certain administrative issues such as names, places of residence, citizenship, registers, holding public gathers and meetings, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us move to Article 5. It is the same page, page 2 in e-court in the B/C/S; and page 1 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to Article 5, who was entrusted with Internal Affairs activities referred to in this article?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Naturally, Article 5 entrusts the ministry with the Internal Affairs; the Ministry of the Interior, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In keeping with this law, in addition to the Ministry of the Interior at headquarters, which other two organisational units were there within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Those were the Public Security and State Security Services.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's talk about the Public Security Service for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us go to Article 15 of the law. In e-court, it is page 3 in the B/C/S, and page 2 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about Article 15. What does it regulate?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Article 15 of the law regulates the competence of the Public Security Service in terms of certain activities and tasks. I won't go into all the detail, but it has to do with administrative and specialised services as one area; another area is protecting law and order and property of the citizens; the third area is crime prevention enforcement; as well as certain societal services, such as dealing with the consequence of states of emergency, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us move to Article 16. I'd like you to focus on the last few lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In e-court, it is page 3 in the B/C/S; in the English version, pages 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We can see here that certain reserve police force members are mentioned. Can you tell me what was the role and position of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: As we can see, Article 16 defines activities in the field of public law and order and property safety of the citizens, as well as combatting crime. It can be done by the active duty policeman, as well as members of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's go to the next article of this law that I want to analyse. It is Article 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is page 4 in the B/C/S in e-court; the same page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you have Article 26 before you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In keeping with the article, except for the ministry at headquarters, which are -- which regional units were there as part of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: In addition to the ministry at headquarters, there were regional units such as Public Security centres, and then the next lower level in territorial terms were Public Security stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us move to Article 28 of the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] page 4 in the B/C/S; in the English, version page 4 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In keeping with Article 28, how many centres of Public Security were there envisaged by the law from 1992, and where?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: According to Article 28, Public Security centres of the MUP were in Banja Luka, Trebinje, Doboj, Sarajevo, and Bijeljina. There were five: Banja Luka, Trebinje, Doboj, Sarajevo, and Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Article 30 is next.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is page 4 in the B/C/S; the same page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What does Article 30 refer to?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Article 30 sets out some other levels of organisation within the MUP. More precisely, it says that police stations are to be set up within Security Services centres, and also a number of reserve police stations. In other words, these police stations and reserve police stations were within the framework of the Public Security station. In the second part of this article, it's last sentence, it says, whenever necessary, i.e., in specific situation, a police station can have its detached squads outside its headquarters. I'm talking about militia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There were smaller organisational units with respect to the police station?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Within the Public Security station, there were police stations and also some detached squads outside --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The word used is "militia." And in Serbian language, words "militia" and "police" are synonymous. So, having in mind that in English word "militia" might have a negative connotation, I would just like to draw your attention to this fact to just in order to avoid any misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Lazarevic. We'll take note of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We will no longer need this document for now. Let us move to the next one. That is tab number 10 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's Exhibit 4D192. That's the set of rules on internal organisation of MUP in the state of an immediate threat of war or a state of war from September 1992. I have to advise Chamber that we do not have the translation of this document, and I think the best approach would be if we continue by reading the relevant paragraphs that I wish to discuss with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, in your report, I have found a piece of information that in April 1992 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- a set of rules were adopted that had the identical title as the one mentioned earlier. Do you know the reason why two set of rules, identical set of rules were adopted on different dates?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Well, the main reason is probably -- well, actually this is identical text. At the bottom of the front page, it reads, "September 1992." And as you can see, in the upper part above, the are words "official secret, strictly confidential." There's a number, 10-3/93, which means that is probably March 1993. So I presume that probably, in March 1993, this set of rules had been debated; and that, in 1992, it was just a draft; and that in the identical form and with the identical wording, it was adopted in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm, please, once again, practically, there are absolutely no differences in the content of these two documents?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Absolutely no difference whatsoever, so it's all the same whichever document you take.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at Article 2 of this set of rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And since we unfortunately do not have translation, I'm going to read it for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Heading of this chapter is Roman numeral II, and it says "Organisational Units." "Appropriate basic and internal organisational units shall be established within the ministry for the purpose of carrying out duties and activities from its purview as follows: Number 1, at the seat of the ministry administration, special police brigade, police detachment, squad, school, inspectorate, section, office, group, and secretariat; number 2, outside the seat-centre, sector, Public Security station, department, police station and station department, section, group, and secretariat." Now, after reading Article 2 of this set of rules, can you explain to me the difference between organisational units intended for carrying out duties in the seat of the ministry and outside the seat of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Well, there are certain organisational units in the seat of the ministry or some forms of organisation that functionally deal with specific problems or they are concentrated on specific areas of interest. However, when we speak about organisational structure of the ministry outside of its seat, that is territorial organisation of units at a lower level than the ones in the ministry itself that we have already mentioned, and these are two main organisational levels outside the seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now move to Article 7 of this set of rules, and I'm going to read it for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The title under Article 7 reads "Organisational Units At the Seat of the Ministry." Article 7: "The following basic organisational units shall be established at the seat of ministry: Number 1, police administration; number 2, administration for prevention and detection of crimes; 3, inspectorate for fire and explosion protection; number 4, administration for analytical and information tasks, and the operation of the IT system; number 5, communications and crypto-protection administration information; number 6, administration for legal, personnel affairs, and issues relating to aliens; number 7, secondary school of Internal Affairs; number 8, administration for financial and technical affairs; and, number 9, office of the minister. Can you tell me what was the nature of these units that we have just listed here?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: All these organisational units that you listed constitute organisational part of the ministry at its seat. So that's the headquarters of the ministry, and we can see --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: And we see that we have functional principle of organising the work processes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I feel that I should apologise for not having the translation of this document. This is the only document that we still haven't been provided with translation. We addressed the CLSS quite a long time ago, but for some reason we still haven't received it. I have to assure that you this is the only one that we don't have a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I understand that we actually have a translated version of it, and I think we can provide that to Defence counsel, if that will assist the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It makes things easier. You've still got another five minutes to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, let us look at Article 8 of this set of rules, and I'm going to read it for the record and, hopefully, tomorrow we shall have an opportunity to work with an English translation which will expedite the process. So, Article 8: "Organisational units referred to items 1 to 3 in the previous article shall be part of the Public Security Service. Organisational units referred to under items 3 to 9, in the previous article, shall carry out other internal and joint affairs." So, pursuant to Article 8, which of these units were part of of the Public Security Service?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Part of the Public Security Service, which is an integral part of the ministry, were police administration, administration for preventing and detecting crime, and in the inspectorate for fire and explosion protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe we should stop now because the next article that I intend to quote to the witness is very long one. It won't be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fine. So we'll continue tomorrow at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 7th day of October 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.22 p.m.
